title: Who wrote this?
explanation: The greeting to Mr. Dube, the short polite tone, and the request to approve a repair all came from naming a writer and a reader. Option D would give a note, but nothing in it says which problem or which floor.
output:
Hi Mr. Dube,

The printer on floor 2 is jammed again. It stops on every second page. Could you approve a repair visit this week? It is slowing the whole team down.

Thanks, Ayesha

options.prompt: Write a note about a broken printer.
You are Ayesha, an office assistant. Your reader is Mr. Dube, a busy manager. Write a short, polite note asking him to approve a repair for the jammed printer on floor 2.
You are a repair technician. Write a note to a printer company asking for parts.
Write a short polite email to my manager about a problem at work.

wrongHint: Look at who the note is to, who it is from, and what it asks for.
